title: Investigate KV/prefix cache hit–conditioned output deltas and implement safety gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Customers and internal canaries have intermittently observed meaningfully different responses when a request hits the KV/prefix cache versus when it misses. These deltas range from small token diffs to semantic shifts that would be visible to downstream apps. Prior tickets explored detection (ENG-4720) and hit-attribution (ENG-19987) but we still lack a robust, deployable plan to quantify, block, and safely roll out cache-related config/model changes that increase hit-conditioned regressions.

Objective:
1) Build an eval harness that exercises production-like prompts and records side-by-side hit vs miss outputs deterministically.
2) Define measurable thresholds (token-level and semantic) to classify a hit-induced delta as acceptable, warning, or blocking.
3) Implement runtime safety gates (metrics + automatic fallbacks) to prevent rollout of cache config or model variants that cause high-impact deltas.
4) Provide dashboards, alerting, and a PR gating checklist for runtime and model changes.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: prefix/KV cache behavior for text generation and chat flows; model variants used in hosted and dedicated clusters; automated detection, gating, and canary rollout hooks.
- Out of scope: full retraining of models, on-device cache changes for private on-prem installs (we will provide guidance but not ship on-prem agents here).

Approach / Plan:
1) Dataset and golden pairs:
   - Assemble a 3k prompt corpus across high-risk customers, internal integrations, and synthetics that stress prefix reuse and streaming scenarios. Use existing golden dataset seeds from ENG-20601 and augment with recent customer traces from March 2026.
   - For each prompt record: (a) canonical miss trace (cold path) and (b) warm/hit trace (KV hit path) with identical model config. Persist both outputs and token-level metadata (logprobs, top-k distributions, KV-hit flag).

2) Deterministic harness and signatureization:
   - Implement a deterministic runner that fixes RNG, batching boundaries, and micro-batching timing to reduce nondeterminism during comparisons.
   - Compute signatures: token-level diff, normalized BLEU-like ngram overlap, embedding cosine similarity (via internal embedding model), and a high-level semantic delta score using instruction-aware evals.

3) Thresholds and classification:
   - Establish three bands: OK (minor token differences, semantic similarity >= 0.98), Warning (semantic similarity between 0.90 and 0.98 OR token diffs concentrated in named entities/formatting), Block (semantic similarity < 0.90 OR user-facing hallucination introduced).
   - Thresholds will be set empirically during the first 2 sprints and validated on holdout prompts.

4) Runtime safety gates and rollout policy:
   - Runtime emits per-request 'hit_delta_score' metric and aggregates a 24h hit-conditioned delta rate.
   - CI/CD gating: model/config changes must run the golden-pairs harness; PRs are blocked if Block-class regressions exceed 0.5% on high-priority prompts or 2% on the full suite.
   - Production fallback: if an autoscaling event or config toggle causes a 1-hour rolling Block-rate > 0.2% on customer-facing clusters, automatically route affected requests to miss-path-compatible model variant (same family, miss-verified) and trigger paging.

5) Observability and triage tooling:
   - Dashboard: per-model, per-route breakdown of hit-rate, hit-conditioned semantic-delta histogram, top failing prompts, and sample diff viewer with side-by-side tokens and logprobs.
   - On-call runbook for investigating hit-conditioned regressions, plus a lightweight A/B diff page for product/SE review.

Acceptance criteria (must be strings):
- "Harness: deterministic side-by-side hit vs miss runner with reproducible outputs for 99% of test runs",
- "Metrics: new runtime metric 'hit_delta_score' emitted for every completed generation",
- "Thresholds: threshold doc published and applied to PR gating policy",
- "Gating: CI blocks PRs that exceed Block-class limits in the golden-pairs run",
- "Fallback: automated routing fallback implemented and tested in canary clusters",
- "Dashboard: triage dashboard with top-100 failing prompts available to SRE/ML/PM teams"
Test plan (high level):
- Local experiments: run harness against 1k curated prompts; iterate on deterministic fixes until variance < 0.5%.
- Canaries: deploy canary config to 5% of traffic with active shadowed runs that compare hit vs miss; measure delta distributions for 72h.
- Staged gating: apply gating to internal dev clusters, then staging, then production following success criteria.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Determinism vs realism: forcing strict determinism in the harness may under-count real-world timing-induced divergences. We'll run both deterministic and 'production-like' noisy runners and compare.
- Cost: running paired miss/hit traces doubles compute for evals; we will schedule nightly windows and sample traffic to limit cost.
- Semantic scorer: embedding-based similarity is fast but may miss subtle instruction-following regressions. We'll keep a small human-eval budget for critical failing prompts.

Implementation Milestones and owners:
- Week 1 (Aisha/Marco): finalize prompt corpus and runner design; PR: github.com/redwood-inference/kv-evals/pull/12.
- Week 2 (Marco): implement deterministic runner + signature extraction; internal PR open for review.
- Week 3 (SRE + Marco): wire runtime metric and lightweight routing fallback prototype.
- Week 4 (Aisha/PM/Product): publish thresholds, create CI gating job and dashboard widgets.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/KV+Hit+Delta+Harnes
- Golden dataset (Drive): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/kv-golden-2026-03
- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-evals/pull/12
- Observability dashboard prototype: https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/kv-hit-delta

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: false positives from thresholding may block harmless performance optimizations. Mitigation: tiered thresholds (warning band) and manual review path to unblock safe changes.
- Risk: added runtime metrics increase telemetry ingress. Mitigation: sample rates and per-customer opt-out.
